steps.title: Position rather than quantity
steps.body: пе́рвый — first. второ́й — second. тре́тий — third. четвёртый — fourth. An ordinal identifies position in an ordered sequence; a cardinal tells how many. These isolated ordinal forms are masculine nominative singular. Learn the position expressed by each form before choosing it.

steps.title: Ordinals agree like adjectives
steps.body: Ordinals agree with their noun in gender, number and case, like adjectives. восемнадцатую девушку means the eighteenth girl as a feminine accusative noun phrase. The retained example comes from a sentence about photographing her; this displayed fragment alone does not mean She just photographed. The ordinal ending follows the noun phrase, rather than staying in the masculine dictionary form. These recognition checks do not assess producing agreement in a sentence.

steps.title: Work the requested position
steps.body: For the first ordinal, choose пе́рвый; for the second ordinal, choose второ́й; for the third ordinal, choose тре́тий. четвёртый expresses fourth, so it fails each of those requests. Read the English request: the separately shown Russian cue may name a different position and is not the target to copy.

sessions.title: Recognize hour counts and noun forms

steps.title: One, two and five hours
steps.body: один час — one hour. два часа — two hours. пять часов — five hours. The noun changes with the count: nominative singular after one, genitive singular after two, and genitive plural after five. English uses hours for both two and five, but Russian uses different forms.

steps.title: Bound the counting rule
steps.body: For basic counts in nominative or inanimate accusative constructions, use the one pattern for numbers ending in 1, the two pattern for endings 2, 3 or 4, and the five pattern for endings 0, 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9. Numbers ending in 11, 12, 13 or 14 take the five pattern instead. Other case constructions require additional changes to the numeral and noun; this is not a rule for every sentence position.

steps.title: Work an hour choice
steps.body: For a two-hour row, choose два часа. один час names one hour and пять часов names five hours. For a five-hour row, choose пять часов, even when the separately shown cue is the one-hour phrase. Read the requested quantity rather than copying the cue. Recognizing these hour counts does not demonstrate telling the time on a clock.

sessions.title: Recognize year counts and noun forms

steps.title: One, two and five years
steps.body: один год — one year. два года — two years. пять лет — five years. The basic counting forms are nominative singular after one, genitive singular after two, and genitive plural after five. The plural counting form for years uses a different stem: learn пять лет as the complete five-year phrase.

steps.title: Compound counts and the teen exception
steps.body: сорок один год — forty-one years. The compound ends in 1, so its noun follows the one pattern. In basic nominative or inanimate accusative counts, endings 2, 3 or 4 follow the two pattern; endings 0 and 5 through 9 follow the five pattern. Endings 11 through 14 are exceptions to the final-digit rule and take the five pattern. Other grammatical cases need additional changes.

steps.title: Work a year choice
steps.body: For a five-year row, choose пять лет, rather than два года, which names two years. For a one-year row, choose один год; for a two-year row, choose два года. The separately shown cue can have a different count. These checks recognize quantities of years, not ordinal calendar-year dates or a complete age sentence.

sessions.title: Recognize minute counts and feminine numerals

steps.title: Minutes use feminine one and two
steps.body: одна минута — one minute. две минуты — two minutes. пять минут — five minutes. The noun for minute is feminine, so one and two use feminine forms here. Compare the masculine hour and year phrases. The noun is nominative singular after one, genitive singular after two, and genitive plural after five.

steps.title: Use the bounded count pattern
steps.body: For basic nominative or inanimate accusative counts, an ending of 1 follows the one-minute pattern, endings 2, 3 or 4 follow the two-minute pattern, and endings 0 or 5 through 9 follow the five-minute pattern. Endings 11 through 14 take the five-minute pattern instead of following the final digit alone. Different case constructions require additional numeral and noun changes.

steps.title: Work a minute choice
steps.body: For a one-minute row, choose одна минута. For a two-minute row, choose две минуты. For a five-minute row, choose пять минут. Each other phrase names a different quantity. Read the English request even if the separately shown cue has a different count. These quantity choices do not assess expressing minutes past an hour on a clock.

steps.title: A person in the dative
steps.body: мне двадцать лет — I am 20 years old. The person whose age is stated is in the dative case: the first word means to me in a literal description. The remaining phrase counts twenty years. The present-time Russian construction has no expressed verb, whereas natural English uses am. This is an age statement, not a statement of ownership.

steps.title: Work the whole phrase and the quantity
steps.body: Compare мне двадцать лет with двадцать лет. The full age statement is I am 20 (years old); the shorter quantity phrase is 20 years and does not by itself identify whose age is meant. The section label age statements names the topic; it is not a translation of either phrase. For a natural-English choice, select I am 20 years old. Ownership of summers and a group of people asking a question would describe different events. These choices recognize this construction; they do not demonstrate independently forming ages for other people or numbers.

steps.title: The first four weekday names
steps.body: понедельник — Monday. вторник — Tuesday. среда — Wednesday. четверг — Thursday. Each word names a day of the week. Match the shown word to its English meaning rather than selecting a neighboring day.

steps.title: Complete the weekday contrast
steps.body: пятница — Friday. суббота — Saturday. воскресенье — Sunday. Together with the previous four names, these make the seven-day set. In the Thursday check, Friday and Saturday are competing day names. In the Sunday check, Monday and Saturday name different days. Learn the Sunday form here before meeting it in an independent check.

steps.title: Capitalization and a worked choice
steps.body: Weekday names normally stay lowercase within a Russian sentence; the first word of a sentence still begins with a capital. For the shown четверг, select Thursday. For the shown воскресенье, select Sunday. Recognizing an isolated name is different from saying on a particular weekday: that use needs its own preposition and case construction, which these checks do not assess.

sessions.title: Distinguish the supplied clock-time and object-selection questions

steps.title: Understand the whole question
steps.body: Который час? — What time is it? This fixed question asks for the current clock time. The noun час normally means hour; its retained example label time reflects this question context rather than a universal translation of the isolated noun. Learn the complete question as a unit.

steps.title: Read the full question and the requested information
steps.body: Forms of который do not by themselves identify a clock question. Read the complete supplied question and its noun. Которое яблоко моё? — Which apple is mine? Asks which apple belongs to the speaker. This is the guided ownership/selection example. Которую книгу вы хотите? — Which book do you want? Asks which book the listener wants. The listener is asked to choose a book. Который час? — What time is it? Asks for the current clock time. This requests the current clock time, not which book the listener wants or which apple belongs to the speaker. The independent clock and book cues are different complete questions from the guided apple cue. These checks recognize the supplied meanings; they do not demonstrate independently asking/giving a new time or forming every interrogative. Optional repeated clock gloss practice is separate from the required checks.

sessions.title: Interpret quarter, half and time remaining

steps.title: A quarter into the next named hour
steps.body: четверть восьмого — 7:15. The eighth hour is the period leading up to eight, not the period starting at eight. A quarter of that hour has elapsed after seven. The ordinal names the next hour and appears in genitive form.

steps.title: Half of the hour in progress
steps.body: полвосьмого — 7:30. Half of the eighth hour has passed, so the clock shows half past seven. The compact half-hour expression is written as one word in this retained form. Match the construction to the clock reading, rather than treating the named eighth hour as the elapsed whole hour.

steps.title: A quarter remaining before eight
steps.body: без четверти восемь — 7:45. This construction counts a quarter hour remaining until eight: subtract fifteen minutes from the named upcoming hour. The without construction differs from counting a quarter or a half already elapsed. These choices interpret existing forms; context is still needed to distinguish morning from evening.

steps.title: Clock readings and event times
steps.body: A current-time question and the time when an event happens are different requests. The retained event sentences use at-time expressions. A preposition introduces several of them, while the without construction expresses minutes remaining until the upcoming hour. Study the complete source examples before selecting their readings.

steps.title: On the hour and contextual AM or PM
steps.body: Концерт начинается в шесть часов. — 18.00. Она была дома в час. — 13.00. These are the readings assigned by the retained source. The bare six-hour and one-hour expressions do not themselves distinguish evening from morning; the source readings depend on context. Do not infer that every occurrence of six means eighteen.

steps.title: Quarter past and the next ordinal
steps.body: Я приду в четверть восьмого. — 7.15 – quarter of the eighth hour. Он нам позвонил в пятнадцать минут десятого. — 9.15 – 15 minutes of the tenth hour. A quarter or fifteen minutes has elapsed in the hour leading to the named next hour. The ordinal is genitive; the event-time phrase also has its introductory preposition.

steps.title: Half past in two retained constructions
steps.body: Наш рейс уезжает в половине пятого. — 4.30 – half of the fifth hour. Мы будем свободны в полвторого. — 1.30 – half of the second hour. Both name a half elapsed in the next ordinal hour. Their retained preposition and noun forms differ; recognize each complete construction rather than exchanging endings mechanically.

steps.title: A quarter before the upcoming hour
steps.body: Передача начинается без четверти три. — 2.45 – 3 without a quarter. Она обычно приходит на работу без пятнадцати девять. — 8.45 – 9 without 15 minutes. Subtract the stated remaining minutes from the upcoming hour. The preposition meaning without governs the remaining quantity in genitive form. These existing choices do not assess independently building a new event-time sentence.

steps.title: Minutes in the hour in progress
steps.body: в пятнадцать минут второго — at 1:15. The second hour runs from one up to two, so fifteen minutes into it is quarter past one. Match this expression to the request for minutes into the hour in progress. The next-hour ordinal is genitive. This convention is used up to the half hour.

steps.title: Minutes remaining after the half hour
steps.body: без двадцати пяти два — at 1:35. Twenty-five minutes remain before two. Subtract the remaining quantity from the upcoming hour. The without construction uses genitive forms for the remaining minutes and differs from counting elapsed minutes.

steps.title: Read the dial numbers
steps.body: в двенадцать часов десять минут — at 12:10. This construction states elapsed whole hours and then minutes, instead of naming an ordinal hour in progress. Reading the dial is always available; context or a 24-hour reading can distinguish AM and PM. These selections identify existing construction types and do not demonstrate independently producing a new clock expression.

sessions.title: Interpret retained dates and year abbreviation

steps.title: Read every part of the date
steps.body: 28 августа 2017 г. gives day month year: 28 August 2017. The abbreviation г. marks the year after its number. 15 мая 1996 г. means 15 May 1996. To translate the whole date, include the day, month and year; identifying only the month or abbreviation leaves part of the meaning out.

steps.title: Month case and date naming
steps.body: Двадцать восьмое августа names the twenty-eighth of August. This standalone date naming uses a neuter ordinal for the day and a genitive month name. A sentence saying when something happens can require a different ordinal case; these checks do not assess that change. The month form in a date differs from its dictionary form. Numeric day-month-year order and the year abbreviation are separate from speaking a complete year in words.

objectives.title: Distinguish which questions from relative clauses

steps.title: Admitted comparison and relative lines
steps.body: Proposed Unit 18 uses admitted comparison lines and admitted relative lines. Qualified review is pending.
steps.bookDirection: Open Lesson 18 in the copy you own. The app records do not replace that lesson.

steps.title: Comparing a quality
steps.body: бо́льший — bigger. лу́чший — better. These retained forms concern degree of a quality, rather than naming an unrelated object. The first compares size. The second is the source gloss used by the existing choice; it can mean best in context, so better here is not a universal translation. These full adjective forms can change for gender, number and case; they are not the same construction as an unchanging short comparative. Qualified review of the contextual gloss remains pending.

steps.title: One-word and two-word comparisons
steps.body: красне́е — redder. бо́лее до́брый — kinder. The first is a short comparative with an ending expressing a higher degree of redness; this short form does not change for gender, number or case. The second combines a word meaning more with the ordinary long adjective meaning kind. In this two-word construction the adjective still changes for agreement. Not every adjective has a one-word comparative, and these examples do not give a complete formation rule for unfamiliar adjectives.

steps.title: Comparative versus superlative
steps.body: наибо́льший — the biggest. This retained superlative identifies the greatest size in the relevant group, rather than just a greater degree. Contrast the source labels бо́лее — more, ме́нее — less, and наиме́нее — least. More and less express comparison; least identifies the lowest degree. For наибо́льший select the biggest, not more or less. For бо́лее до́брый select kinder, not least or bigger. These choices recognize existing forms; they do not assess independently forming new comparisons or a complete comparison sentence.

sessions.title: Distinguish which questions from relative clauses

steps.title: Questions selecting an apple or a book
steps.body: Которое яблоко моё? — Which apple is mine? Которую книгу вы хотите? — Which book do you want? These are direct questions asking which member is selected, not relative clauses modifying an earlier noun. In the apple question the selecting form agrees with a neuter singular subject in the nominative. In the book question it agrees with a feminine singular direct object in the accusative. Match the whole question: ownership of an apple differs from wanting a book.

steps.title: A relative clause adds information about a noun
steps.body: Человек, который изменил мир — The man who changed the world. The clause following the comma describes the preceding person; it does not ask which person. The relative form takes masculine singular agreement from that noun, and nominative case because it is the subject of changed inside its own clause. For a relative form, gender and number come from the noun it describes; case comes from the role inside the relative clause, not automatically from the preceding noun.

steps.title: With whom: a preposition inside the relative clause
steps.body: Же́нщина, с кото́рой я дружу́ — The woman (who) I'm friends with. The relative clause describes the woman. Its relative form has feminine singular agreement and instrumental case after the preposition meaning with. Russian keeps this preposition before the relative form, while the retained English rendering places with at the end. Compare the woman described by friendship with the man described by changing the world and the two direct questions. Recognizing these meanings does not demonstrate independently choosing a relative case or producing a new clause.
